solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clansman regularly drinks a French wine or port

indicators.note: whoever drinks something takes it inside, so these letters go into the others
taking every other letter of Clansman, starting from the first, picks out a regular sequence

parts.note: blanc is French for white, as in vin blanc, white wine

explanation.surface: A Scottish clansman knocks back a French white or a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clansman regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters; the wine goes in just before the last of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Casablanca is Morocco's chief seaport on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Dismissive remark by solicitor — this involves penalties

parts.note: shoo is what you say to send someone or something away
a tout solicits custom, for tickets or business

explanation.surface: A lawyer makes a dismissive comment, and the talk is of legal penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is anyone who solicits trade: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: A football match level after extra time is settled by a penalty shootout, a series of spot kicks.

clue.text: Where paella's served, Russian removes covering of tin

indicators.note: the outer letters of the Russian word are stripped away, and they spell the chemical symbol for tin

parts.note: a Siberian is a Russian from Siberia
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A Russian in a Spanish restaurant peels the lid off a tin of paella.
explanation.walkthrough: SIBERIAN begins with S and ends with N, the symbol for tin; removing that covering leaves the peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish, served across the Iberian peninsula of Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Harry getting track that's a hit rock'n'roll song

parts.note: to harry is to pursue relentlessly, to hound
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: Someone named Harry records a track that becomes a rock'n'roll hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Hound Dog was Elvis Presley's huge 1956 hit record, first recorded by Big Mama Thornton.

clue.text: Extremely boastful German fellow is loaded

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of boastful are used, its first and last

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A bragging German man is very rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' suggests wealth, but it is slang for drunk; 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier but picks the ends of boastful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for heavily drunk.

clue.text: Leaders of English grenadiers gleefully attack fragile structure

indicators.note: the leaders of the three following words are their opening letters

parts.note: to shell is to attack with artillery

explanation.surface: English grenadiers happily bombard some flimsy building.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg's shell is the classic thin, easily broken casing; we speak of walking on eggshells.

clue.text: A child of Jacob's in some parties

indicators.note: read as a verb, parties means splits up and separates, so the letters of these words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: One of Jacob's children turns up at several parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' looks like a noun for gatherings, but is the verb meaning splits up, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Simeon was the second son of Jacob and Leah in Genesis, ancestor of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Console revolutionary for a long time

indicators.note: something that revolves turns around, so the brand name is read backwards

parts.note: Sega is a brand of video-game console

explanation.surface: A game console that revolutionises things for years to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like the verb to comfort, but it is the games machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially 'for ages' means a very long period, as in waiting ages for a bus.

clue.text: People keeping dry and hot — how satisfying!

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, helps people stay off drink, keeping dry
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with pleasure at keeping dry and warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping dry' suggests staying out of rain; here it means abstaining from alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a contented sigh of pleasure or relief.

clue.text: Requesting to pocket loot, involved in illicit trade

indicators.note: something that pockets another takes it inside, so the jumbled loot goes into the asking word

parts.note: begging means asking or requesting earnestly

indicators.note: involved in the sense of tangled or intricate, so the letters of loot are mixed up

explanation.surface: Pleading to keep stolen goods while caught up in smuggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' means tangled, so it scrambles the stolen goods, which then go just after the first letter of the asking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootlegging is the illegal making or smuggling of goods, originally alcohol during Prohibition.

clue.text: Casanova mournfully admits love affair

indicators.note: the phrase lets in, contains, the letters running across its two words

explanation.surface: The famous seducer sadly confesses to an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means a romantic liaison, often a secret one.

clue.text: Revised stats seen showing what a business owns

indicators.note: the letters of stats and seen are revised, reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Updated figures reveal a company's holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounting term for total assets minus liabilities, the value a company actually holds.

clue.text: Clingy garment stars darn the wrong way

parts.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: reading the curse the wrong way means backwards

parts.note: darn and drat are both mild curses

explanation.surface: Someone mends a stretchy outfit with stars on it backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darn' looks like mending but is a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a skin-tight one-piece worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Concerned with the main cocaine supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, meaning flexibly, so the letters of cocaine are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A smuggling ring dealing in drugs shipped by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, as in drug supply, but is read as 'supplely', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old poetic word for the open sea, so oceanic means relating to it.

clue.text: Pope wearing top of eye-catching orange

parts.note: Clement is the name of fourteen popes
you are in clothes you are wearing

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Pope sports a striking orange outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orange' looks like a colour, but it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small sweet citrus fruit, a type of mandarin orange.

clue.text: New tech billionaire cutting the BS after working tonight in London location

indicators.note: the trimmed billionaire is placed after the rearranged word
working letters are being worked over, rearranged
the billionaire is cutting out, dropping, the two named letters

parts.note: Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft
the letters B and S, also slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A newly rich tech mogul drops the nonsense after a night's work in a smart part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: TONIGHT rearranged gives OTTINGH; BILL GATES without its B and S gives ILL GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Notting Hill Gate is a district and Tube station in west London.

clue.text: Where policemen work, gents uncovered case

parts.note: detectives work in the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department

indicators.note: with its covering of first and last letters taken off

explanation.surface: A police station gents' toilet becomes a crime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an event or occurrence, especially one police deal with, so a case.

clue.text: Confiscates £1,000,000?

parts.note: the figure read as one, M for million, then the currency word gives a verb for seizing goods; I is the Roman one

explanation.surface: Authorities seize a million pounds of someone's money.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the sum literally as I (one) M (million) and pounds, and the letters spell the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound is to seize and hold property by legal authority.

clue.text: What stops a scoundrel in old-fashioned pub

indicators.note: the question stops a gap, plugging the inside of the other letters

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person
eh? is said when you have not heard, like what?

explanation.surface: Something halts a villain in an old-style tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the start of a question; it is EH, the query.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is the dated term for a tavern selling beer.

clue.text: Fruit in spring period — it keeps firm

parts.note: Apr is the calendar abbreviation for April, a spring month

indicators.note: the word it holds the firm inside it

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Fruit picked in spring stays firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a description of fruit, but it is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit related to the peach.

clue.text: Plan to get fit for government

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exercise or diet routine
second meaning: a system or period of rule

explanation.surface: A government workout scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fitness or diet routine and a ruling administration, especially an authoritarian one.

clue.text: In Paris you read in Italian

parts.note: tu is the familiar French for you
to scan is to read over quickly

explanation.surface: A French speaker reads a book in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan comes from Tuscany, a region of central Italy.

clue.text: Rubbish, say, in vacuous programme — The Apprentice

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the emptied word
vacuous means empty, so programme loses its middle letters

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A critic calls the TV show The Apprentice an empty, trashy programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Apprentice' looks like the TV title; only 'Apprentice' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone guided and trained by a mentor, a pupil or trainee.

clue.text: Fought like a knight, getting decapitated and unseated

indicators.note: losing its head means losing the first letter

parts.note: knights jousted with lances on horseback

explanation.surface: A knight jousts, has his head cut off and falls from the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to remove from office, and in jousting the loser is unseated from the horse.

clue.text: Cat has gold-plated bowl, which is capital

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat

indicators.note: gold plating covers the dish, so its letters go around those of the bowl

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a dish is a bowl

explanation.surface: A cat eating from a fancy gilded bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold-plated' is two signals: the gold symbol, then plating that wraps it round the bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Mogadishu is the capital city of Somalia.

clue.text: Ruin end of break one once spent in Berlin

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: the end of break is its last letter

explanation.surface: A holiday in Berlin is spoilt at the end of the break.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro, so it was spent in Berlin.

clue.text: Someone who should be prepared visits Coutts banks

indicators.note: to bank is to hold or keep, so the two words keep the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A prudent person goes to Coutts, the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Coutts is an old private bank in London, famously the Queen's; 'Be prepared' is the Scout motto.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouts are pledged to their motto Be Prepared, so a member should always be ready.

clue.text: Love affair round foreign land? It goes off with a bang

definitions.text: It goes off with a bang

indicators.note: the love affair goes round the jumbled land

parts.note: a romance is a love affair

indicators.note: foreign means strange or out of place, so land is rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday romance in a strange country ends explosively.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled land sits inside the love affair just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman candle is a firework that shoots out balls of fire with bangs.

clue.text: What tumble-dryers do after losing power function

indicators.note: the action word loses the named letter

parts.note: tumble-dryers spin clothes
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A tumble-dryer stops working after a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like the dryer working; it is the trigonometric sine, written sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sin is the mathematical abbreviation for sine, a trigonometric function.
